title: Why passwords are often stored in char[] instead of String
answer: A `char[]` is often preferred for temporary in-memory password handling because the application can overwrite the array after use, reducing how long the characters remain intentionally reachable in memory. A `String` is immutable, so its character content cannot be overwritten in place and may remain until garbage collection; additional String copies can also be created by normal operations. A `char[]` is not a perfect security guarantee because runtimes and libraries may create copies internally, but it gives the application more control. Passwords should never be interned, logged, or unnecessarily converted to String.
